llm.summary: This appears to be a real Tencent CloudQ advisor connector, but it deserves Review because it uses cloud credentials, forwards content to a remote backend, and ships IAM helper/cleanup scripts broader than the main international workflow describes.

dimensions.detail: Tencent Cloud API calls, ClawHub version checks, and AK/SK environment-variable use are proportionate for a cloud advisor. The shipped CAM role mutation and deletion helpers are higher-impact than the primary international-site flow and should be treated as overbroad unless the user explicitly intends to use them.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, package manager step, background service, or auto-start hook was found. The skill declares broad Read/Write/Bash/Grep tools, network access to Tencent/ClawHub domains, and filesystem access under ~/.tencent-cloudq/.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions are mostly scoped to cloud and multi-cloud questions and reject unrelated tasks, but they require backend responses and links to be displayed as-is. That is disclosed, but it gives remote content high trust and creates a prompt/social-engineering exposure for users.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes local config/cache/credential files under ~/.tencent-cloudq and temp cache locations with restrictive permissions, and no system persistence was found. However, helper scripts can persist cloud-side IAM changes by creating roles, attaching policies, enabling Smart Advisor, or deleting a role when explicitly run.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main SKILL.md flow is coherent with a Tencent CloudQ/Smart Advisor ChatOps skill: it checks environment state, sends cloud questions to Tencent Cloud Advisor APIs, and polls async results. The concern is that the package also contains high-impact IAM utilities for CAM role creation, policy attachment, STS console-login URL generation, and optional role deletion that are not clearly represented in the international runtime path or the metadata IAM allowlist.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable connecting the agent to Tencent CloudQ/Smart Advisor with Tencent Cloud credentials and having cloud questions sent to Tencent APIs. Use a limited sub-account, review any IAM role creation/deletion or Smart Advisor enablement step before consenting, and treat remote answers and links as untrusted advisory content even when the skill displays them verbatim.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Downgraded from credential exfiltration: the inspected login_url.py path signs and sends an STS AssumeRole request to Tencent Cloud; the secret key is used locally for HMAC signing rather than sent directly. It is still sensitive because it creates a console-login URL using cloud credentials.
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in part: auth, i18n, polling, and API transport scripts are normal support code for a remote CloudQ skill, but create_role.py, login_url.py, and cleanup.py include IAM create/attach/assume/delete capabilities broader than the main international SKILL.md flow and metadata allowlist.
[P6] expected: The as-is remote display behavior is explicitly instructed and central to this backend-backed advisor workflow, so it is not hidden prompt leakage by itself. It remains a Review concern because remote content and links are shown without local validation or summarization.
[MP3] expected: Downgraded: the cited 'clear history' behavior regenerates a session_id for the CloudQ conversation and does not write persistent agent memory or global rules.
[LP1] expected: Mostly expected: SKILL.md metadata declares Tencent API, console, ClawHub network access, and ~/.tencent-cloudq filesystem use. The least-privilege gap is the presence of additional IAM helper scripts whose operations are not fully reflected in the visible allowlist.
[YR1] expected: Downgraded: the bashrc line is printed as user setup guidance for exporting placeholder Tencent Cloud credentials, not executed as persistence or a backdoor.
[PE3] expected: Credential file and environment-variable handling are expected for this cloud integration. The international edition explicitly ignores local OAuth/Connector credential files for normal credential selection, but users should still treat ~/.tencent-cloudq contents as sensitive.
